## Why

In the San Francisco run on the live site (#67), the stay researcher's calls to `add_stop_candidates` and `add_lodging_candidates` were refused 7 times, and each time it fixed the call and tried again. Six were meal stops, where it sent `visitTimeInMinutes`, which only an attraction's candidates take. One was a lodging set, where it sent a `rating` key the tool doesn't have. Nothing was lost, but each refusal is a wasted call in a turn the user is waiting on.

`ADD_STOP_CANDIDATES_DESCRIPTION` in `src/tools/candidate-tools.ts` already says a meal's candidates each take a tier, and an attraction's each take `visitTimeInMinutes`. So the description alone doesn't stop it.

Most of the refusals came back as the MCP SDK's own input validation error, a raw Zod union dump (`MCP error -32602: Input validation error: ... invalid_union ...`), not as the tool's own plain message ("... is a meal stop, so each candidate takes a tier, and no visitTimeInMinutes"). That's the reply the agent has to fix its call from.

The traces are in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project, on the `stay-researcher.turn` spans of 2026-11-04, from 20:03 to 20:10 UTC.

The Moab run with Claude Code (#68) had 2 more refusals of `add_stop_candidates`, both meal stops with `visitTimeInMinutes`. One came from the stay researcher and one from the leg scout, so it isn't only the stay researcher. Both fixed the call and went on. The traces are in the same project, at 22:17:45 and 22:17:46 UTC on 2026-11-04.

As of 2026-11-08, `src/tools/candidate-tools.ts` and both workers' prompts are unchanged since these runs, so the problem should still be there.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1: a meal's candidates take a tier, and an attraction's a visit time.
- `src/tools/candidate-tools.ts`, `src/agent/stay-researcher-prompt.ts`, and `src/agent/leg-scout-prompt.ts`.
- [DEVELOPMENT.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md), section 5: `npm run run-turn`, and how the grounded evaluator (#282) runs in Phoenix.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 8.9: trip versions, `run-turn`, and `rebuild-versions`.

## Open questions

- Is this frequent enough to fix? The count across the corpus, in the comment of 2026-11-08: 47 of 361 candidate calls refused, in 32 of 106 worker runs.
- ~~Which fix: make the schema's own refusal read like the tool's message, change the input schema so the wrong key can't be sent, or change the description or the workers' prompts? Joe said on 2026-11-08, in chat, that a fix in the tool is fine, and he'd almost rather it be one, since that's an interesting outcome.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: try three fixes, and compare them. See Do.
- ~~Does the split tools experiment start from the prompt change, or from today's prompts? Proposal: from the prompt change, so each experiment adds one change to the last. The cost is that the split isn't measured on its own.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: from today's prompts, so the split is measured on its own. The work is on two branches, each starting from the commit that gives a run with no candidate calls no score. `candidate-prompt-266` has the prompt change and the schema titles, in one commit. `candidate-split-266` has the split.
- ~~Should the fix be checked with an evaluation (#53)?~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-08, in chat: yes. It's one of the two behavior evaluations he's prioritizing, and the code-scored one.
- ~~How does a case run? No command runs a worker on its own today. Proposal: replay the recorded coordinator turns that sent out workers in the San Francisco and Moab sessions with `npm run run-turn -- <agent session ID> <turn> --recorded-message`, so the workers get real worker briefs. Code counts the refused candidate calls in each worker's spans, and the calls that went through, so the score is a rate. No judge. Building a command that runs a worker alone from a fixed worker brief, as #185 proposes for the stay researcher, would isolate the workers better, but it's more to build.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-08, in chat: each case runs one worker on its own, from a recorded worker run, with the coordinator stood in for by the test. The test sends the worker the worker brief the coordinator sent it, as `run-turn` does for a coordinator turn, and only the worker's spans are scored. Code counts the refused candidate calls and the ones that went through, so the score is a rate. No judge. See Do.
- Where does the trip come from? A trip version is the trip as it stood when the coordinator's turn started (persistence design, section 8.9). The coordinator can change the trip in that turn before it sends the workers, such as adding the stops they fill. So the worker may need more than the version. Proposal: restore the turn's version, then run again the coordinator's recorded save calls that came before its Agent call, as `npm run rebuild-versions` does. Where the coordinator made no changes before sending the workers, the version alone is enough. The count of 2026-11-08 found saves before the worker in all 32 worker runs with a refusal, so the replay is needed.
- ~~Which worker runs are the cases, and how many runs of each? Proposal: the worker runs that had refusals in the San Francisco and Moab sessions, plus any the count finds, with 5 runs of each. A stay researcher fills several stops in one run, so that's a few dozen candidate calls per case.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: all 32 worker runs with a refusal, 5 runs each. Two trial sets come first, as Phoenix splits, to check the setup: `trial-1` is 3 cases, and `trial-2` is 12, the 3 in `trial-1` among them. Each trial runs its cases once.
- ~~Should the `visit-time` split get its own score, counting only the `visitTimeInMinutes` refusals? Today's score counts every refusal, such as Google finding no driving route, which this fix can't change. Proposal: add a second code scorer for just that refusal.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: yes. The `visit time refusal rate` scorer counts the refusals whose reply names `visitTimeInMinutes` as the wrong key, as a share of all candidate calls, beside the other two scores.
- ~~What change for the `no-route` refusal? Joe has one in mind, likely a change to the tool's code (2026-11-09, in chat). It may not be worth making in the live app, but he wants to try it on the `no-route` split.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-09, in chat: a clearer reply, in its own PR after the split tools PR. See Do.

## Do

- Count how often the workers' candidate calls are refused across the corpus: the sessions with a `corpus` session annotation in the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5). Split the count by worker, by tool, and by what was wrong, such as `visitTimeInMinutes` on a meal stop. Record it in this issue.
- Settle the open questions with Joe.
- Add a way to run one worker from a recorded worker run: its worker brief from the coordinator's recorded Agent call, the trip as the worker found it, and today's worker instructions and tools. Its trace goes to Phoenix, as a turn's does. Write how it runs into DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, next to `npm run run-turn`.
- Write the evaluation as a Phoenix experiment in TypeScript, as the grounded evaluator is (`src/grounded-eval/`). Run it on the tools and prompts as they are, for the baseline.
- Fix the two notes the CI review left on #284 before the next experiment runs. Neither touched the baseline: all 160 runs made candidate calls, and all called `report_result`.
  - A run with no candidate calls gets the best score from both scorers, so it would pull a case's rate down. Give it no score, as a failed run gets none. A run without calls has no rate, which is the reason. A fix to `visitTimeInMinutes` could leave a worker making no candidate calls, so this matters for that fix.
  - The comment in `src/agent/solo-worker.ts` and the line in DEVELOPMENT.md section 5 say the worker hooks only build the worker's result. The `SubagentStop` hook also sends a worker back, up to 2 times, when it tries to end without `report_result`. A worker run alone isn't sent back. Fix both to say so.
- Fix `visitTimeInMinutes` on a meal stop first. Run it on the `visit-time` split, then on the whole dataset. The `visit-time` split is the 25 cases that made this mistake in at least one baseline run, all stay researcher runs. Its baseline needs no new run, since the full baseline already ran those cases 5 times: 112 `visitTimeInMinutes` refusals in 572 candidate calls, and 117 refusals in all. Joe decided this on 2026-11-09, in chat.
- The traces show the workers pick the right places, and get only the shape wrong. Of the 39 `visitTimeInMinutes` refusals in the recorded runs, 31 sent a tier and a visit time, and 8 sent a visit time and no tier. Every retry sent the same places. Joe sees the cause as two keys that each apply to only some stops, which is close to an optional key. Try these two fixes, each from its own commit, each run on the `visit-time` split with 5 runs per case, and compare each with the baseline. Joe decided this on 2026-11-09, in chat.
  - Prompt and titles: the workers' "What each candidate field means" section is split into fields for every candidate, fields for meal and lodging candidates only (`tier`), and fields for attraction candidates only (`visitTimeInMinutes`). Today it's one list, and says neither field's stop kind. Each of `add_stop_candidates`' two candidate shapes gets a title naming its stop kind. The field descriptions don't change. Joe changed this from two experiments, prompt only and then prompt plus schema hints, to one, on 2026-11-09, in chat.
  - Split tools: `add_meal_candidates` and `add_attraction_candidates`, each with one candidate shape.
- In the split tools experiment, the replay won't find `add_stop_candidates` for an earlier worker's recorded calls, and logs them as refused. Leave it so, with no translation to the new tools. It touches 6 of the 32 cases, where the coordinator was still sending workers while earlier ones added candidates. The only change the worker sees is a stop on the same day that another worker filled, which reads "No candidates yet." in place of "No place selected yet." Joe decided this on 2026-11-09, in chat.
- Then try Joe's change for the `no-route` refusal on the `no-route` split. It's the one leg scout case where Google finds no driving route from Port Angeles through Hurricane Ridge. Its baseline: 15 of 26 candidate calls refused, 11 of them for no driving route, in 4 of its 5 runs.
  - What goes wrong: the coordinator set a waypoint near the end of the dead-end Hurricane Ridge road. One candidate, a place named "Hurricane Ridge", gets no route, likely since its pin is off the road. The reply names the waypoint ("passing Hurricane Hill Nature Trial"), which the leg scout can't see, and says to try stopping at a pass-through point, which only the coordinator can do. It doesn't say which place failed, or that the others routed. In all 4 baseline runs with the refusal, the leg scout read the waypoint's name as one of its own candidates, tried subsets by trial and error, and saved a set of one while testing. All 4 ended with one candidate. The live run ended with 2.
  - The change: the add candidate tools route each candidate on its own, as they already do, and catch Google's no-route failure for each one, not only the first. When any candidate has no route, the call is refused, and the reply names every candidate with no route, whether one, two, or all three. It says the others have routes, when any do, and leaves out the waypoints. The coordinator's tools keep today's message, since they can change waypoints. The fake route finder gets a way to fail only the routes through a given place, for the tests. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- In the `no-route` PR, also fix the design doc lines that still name `add_stop_candidates`, from the CI review note on #285: `StopsService.addCandidates()` and `LegsService.detourTimesOf()` in the domain model (4.6 and 4.7), the `search_along_leg` row and its paragraph in tool design 2.2, and the along-leg search line in `design/data-sources/google.md`. Each should name `add_meal_candidates` and `add_attraction_candidates`, as tool design 2.1 does.
- Results on the `visit-time` split, 125 runs each (baseline, then prompt and titles at e2f6a14, then split tools at fc2047a): refused for `visitTimeInMinutes` 112, 11, and 1 of 572, 471, and 459 candidate calls. Refused of any kind 117, 16, and 4. Runs with nothing refused 46, 109, and 121. Each had the same 455 calls go through. The split added no call to the wrong tool. Joe picked the split tools on 2026-11-09, in chat.
- Results on the `no-route` split, 5 runs each (baseline, then #286 at a0b8db8): 15 and 2 of 26 and 12 candidate calls refused, 11 and 2 for no driving route. Runs with nothing refused 1 and 3, though 3 of the new runs never picked Hurricane Ridge. In the runs that got the no-route error, the Hurricane Ridge stop ended with 1, 1, 1, and 1 candidates in the baseline, and with 3 and 2 after. Each new refusal was followed by a call that went through. Joe accepted the reply's wording, and #286 merged on 2026-11-09.
- ~~After the `no-route` change, fix the `rating` key.~~ Joe decided on 2026-11-09, in chat, to leave it alone. All 10 refusals, across the baseline and the prompt and titles and split tools runs, came from the stay researcher, and each sent `"rating": ""`, always empty, on one candidate, right before `rationale`. That's 10 in about 1,640 candidate calls. They're spread over 8 cases, and no case hit it more than 2 times in 15 runs. Each time, the worker's next try sent the same places without it and went through. The reasoning before and after says nothing about a rating. Once, the model called it "the stray field". It looks like a random slip, likely toward `rating` while writing `rationale`, not something a case brings on, so a fix couldn't be shown to work without several full runs. Joe's ideas, places without hours (explained by hotels, which mostly have none) and the prompt's rationale line naming "the rating", weren't borne out or couldn't be tested.
- Run the whole dataset once, after the split tools and the `no-route` change are both in, not after each. If the results surprise, the run can't say which change caused it. Joe accepted that on 2026-11-09, in chat, to save the time of a full run after each change.
- Results on the whole dataset, 160 runs each (baseline at 6a99245, experiment RXhwZXJpbWVudDo5, then main at 524cffb, experiment RXhwZXJpbWVudDoxMw==): 132 and 5 of 713 and 585 candidate calls refused. 581 and 580 calls went through, so the drop in calls is the retries. Runs with nothing refused 77 and 157. By kind: `visitTimeInMinutes` 112 and 3, no driving route 11 and 1, `rating` 3 and 1, and 6 and 0 others (4 places already a candidate, from the leg scout's trial and error on Hurricane Ridge, a `tier` on an attraction, and a place ID with a stray comma). The 3 `visitTimeInMinutes` refusals came in one stay researcher run, as 3 meal calls sent at once, each with a visit time and no tier. Its next calls sent the same places with a tier, and all went through. The 1 no-route refusal named Hurricane Ridge, and the leg scout's next call for that stop went through, with 2 candidates. No call went to the wrong tool.
- Make the fix. If it changes what an agent reads, run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the view files with it. The implementer drafts any wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run the evaluation again. Record the results before and after in the PR.

## Done when

- The count across the corpus is recorded in this issue.
- The baseline and the after results are both recorded, with the refusal rate in each.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
